findings.evidence: publication_queue.py:1331 treats any moved head over a READMISSION_STATES record as awaiting re-admission. :1582-1583 sets next_action to 'developer re-admission: rerun finish for the pushed head'. design.md Risks admits this and says the handoff is refused while the claim is live. The status and next_action text is still misleading for a claimed finalize. _awaiting_readmission could skip the report when the finalize job holds a live claim.
findings.summary: Adding finalize-pending to READMISSION_STATES makes a normal in-flight coordinator finalize (push landed, update not yet recorded) look like a head awaiting developer re-admission, and candidate_from_snapshot then tells the developer to rerun finish.

findings.evidence: publication_queue.py:1211 `_awaits_developer_fix` checks state membership only. The live-claim guard sits in _supersession. A developer can therefore have the archived change re-opened locally and then be refused at handoff. The new tests cover the claim refusal only through admit, not through the local_status path.
findings.summary: DEVELOPER_FIX_STATES now includes finalize-pending, so local_status and semantic_readmission accept and re-open an archived change for a descendant head without checking for a live finalize claim. The claim refusal only happens later in admit.
